\begin{example} \end{example}[Another Smooth Structure on $\mathbb {R}$]

1. ch1:1.23The homeomorphism \[ \psi :\mathbb R\to \mathbb R,\qquad \psi (x)=x^3 \tag {1.1} \] determines a smooth structure using the one-chart atlas $(\mathbb R,\psi )$. It differs from the standard structure because the transition $\psi ^{-1}(y)=y^{1/3}$ is not smooth at $0$. More generally, every positive-dimensional topological manifold that admits one smooth structure admits uncountably many distinct smooth structures. \end{example}
